per_turn.simulated_user_message:
I let out a quiet laugh, shaking my head slightly as I set my glass down on the coffee table between us. "Well, I'm glad I accidentally did something right, then."

I lean back into the couch, turning my body a little more toward her—not closing the distance, but making it clear I'm here, I'm present, I'm not going anywhere yet.

"And for the record," I add, meeting her gaze and holding it, "I meant what I said about the wine. But I'd have come anyway. I just wouldn't have had the courage to say that out loud an hour ago."

I pause, then let myself smile—small, honest, a little crooked to match hers.

"So. What do we do with this 'next hour' that's gonna determine whether tonight was a mistake?"

I pick up my glass again and take a slow sip, buying myself a second to let the weight of her words settle. The rain fills the silence between us, steady and unhurried, and I realize I don't want to rush this either.

I set the glass back down and shift on the couch—just enough to close some of the distance between us, my knee now a few inches from where her foot rests on the cushion. Close, but still leaving her the space to decide what happens next.

"Honestly?" I say, and my voice comes out quieter than I expected, like the room got smaller. "I've spent the last hour talking myself out of coming here. Telling myself it was just wine, just small talk, just—" I stop, shake my head. "But I'm sitting on your couch in a stranger's apartment at—" I glance at the clock on the wall, "—whatever ungodly hour this is, and I'm not thinking about the weather."

I let myself look at her fully then—not darting away, not performing confidence I don't feel. Just looking.

"So yeah. I'm thinking about the same thing. I just didn't want to be the one to say it first and have you realize I'm not worth the risk."

I hold her gaze, steady, and wait.
